domain: Node.js MCP adapter/shim layer correctness — local-first data-serving contracts that must reproduce a retired service's response shape field-for-field
axioms: A retired remote API's response shape is a contract every existing caller already depends on; the local replacement must reproduce it field-for-field, not just 'equivalently.'
The only ground truth for 'what a caller reads' is the caller's own code (index.js/cli.js handlers), never a plan's prose description of it.
A lexical/embedding search or resolution function is judged by what it returns for adversarial inputs (name collisions, missing fields, corrupt records), not just its happy-path test.
An error path that returns undefined/null/throws where the caller expects `{success:false, error}` breaks the caller identically to a wrong success value — both are contract violations.
A fallback tier (embedding to lexical, local Ollama to remote) is only safe if the caller can tell which tier answered; an unlabeled fallback is a silent quality regression.
Counting claims in a spec (e.g. '17 names', '18 names') are themselves falsifiable against the actual source file and must be checked, not trusted.
failure_mode: Cross-language parity between embed.js and harvest/embed.py's Python semantics — that comparison belongs to a sibling lens's domain, not this one.
Whether the underlying graph algorithms (centrality, paths, bridges) in graph.js are correct — this lens treats graph.js as a black box the way api-local.js does.
Distributed/multi-machine record-identity questions (accretive index, dedupe across harvests) that live in the harvest package's own domain.
Filesystem/git-level execution risk in the prune sweep, or zklw's actual current host state.
